scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw MD trajectories is infeasible in the verifier; result-level comparison with paper gold and structural monotonicity/saturation checks provide verifiable scoring.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold anisotropic thermal conductivity values at 200,300,400,500 K from paper text and Fig. 3b
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text explicitly states κ[100]=10.68, κ[010]=20.78, κ[001]=12.61 at 300 K. Values at 200, 400, 500 K were read from Fig. 3b (NNP‑EMD solid symbols) and rounded to one decimal place, ensuring consistency with the trends. They match the reference solve.sh.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Direct extraction from paper for 300 K; for other temperatures, values were interpolated from the plotted curves and rounded.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own numerical results for the same anisotropic lattice thermal conductivity computed by the NNP‑EMD method; the tolerance (±1.0 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) is wide enough to accommodate honest re‑run with a different NNP instance or MD settings but narrow enough to reject random numbers.

hidden_assets.purpose: Saturation values for modal accumulation curves (total κ[100], κ[010], κ[001] at 300 K)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 4 shows accumulated κ curves that saturate at the total thermal conductivity values (10.68, 20.78, 12.61). By definition, modal accumulation sums to the total κ at infinite frequency.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Same values as the total κ at 300 K from the paper text.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The saturation values are physically required to be the total thermal conductivity; they are the same numbers reported by the paper for total κ.

outputs.description: Anisotropic lattice thermal conductivity values of β‑Ga₂O₃ along three crystallographic directions at 200, 300, 400, and 500 K.
Accumulated lattice thermal conductivity as a function of phonon mode frequency at 300 K for the three crystallographic directions.

output_contract.notes: The checker will compare the agent-reported thermal conductivity values and accumulated curves to the paper’s published results within appropriate tolerances. Exact gold values and tolerances are hidden.

steps.scoring: max_abs_error across all 12 values; if max_abs_error <= tolerance, score=1.0; else score = max(0.0, 1.0 - (max_abs_error - tolerance) / 2.0).

Combined: monotonicity (0.4 weight) and saturation (0.6 weight). Monotonicity score = 1.0 if all three directions never decrease; else 0.0. Saturation score = fraction of directions whose final accumulated κ is within ±15% of gold_saturation.
